question.text: What is the purpose of ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount) in a public issue?

answer.text: To block the application money in the investor's bank account and release funds only upon allotment
To transfer the application money immediately to the company's account
To allow investors to apply without any payment
To deduct money from the investor's demat account

explanation.text: The Logic: Under ASBA, the investor authorises the bank to block the application money in the investor's own bank account. The funds remain blocked until allotment: on allotment the bank debits the account to the extent of shares allotted, and any remaining blocked amount is released back to the investor. The Trap: Option (b) describes the pre-ASBA system where money was transferred upfront. Option (c) is wrong because some payment commitment (in the form of a block) is always required. Option (d) is wrong because ASBA blocks bank-account funds, not demat holdings. Note: Workbook references: NISM Series XII pp.95 and 98-99 explain ASBA's block/release mechanism; p.99 covers UPI-based ASBA being available for retail applications up to Rs. 5 lakh.
